title: S3-TTA: Scale-Style Selection for Test-Time Augmentation in Biomedical Image Segmentation
mechanism: For each test image, choose the scale and style transform whose prediction is most consistent under further transforms, instead of averaging all views.
adaptation: Per cell, choose among scales 0.75 to 1.5 and gamma 0.8/1/1.25 by flip-consistency of the crack + inactive probability maps. This targets the per-source contrast differences (5 sources) and BMRK scale. Pure inference on existing checkpoints.
min_experiment: Arm: per-cell scale+gamma selection on FINAL. Baselines: FINAL plain and with D4 TTA. Metrics: per-source crack IoU (BMRK, CFVS, CSIR), overall crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill if no source gains >= +0.02 and overall crack IoU is not up >= +0.005.
evidence: R: +3.4% over prior art on cell segmentation and +1.3% on lung segmentation.
prior_overlap: None for per-image scale/style selection. Intensity normalisation failed (BRIEF s5), but that was a fixed global mapping, not per-cell selection by consistency.
